results.title: Pyber's conjecture for finite simple groups (Kourovka 20.74(a))

results.title: Run lengths of a digit list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a list $b_1, \dots, b_k$ of natural numbers (binary digits) and a natural number $c$, this is the list, in order of occurrence, of the lengths of the maximal runs of $1$s in the sequence consisting of $c$ ones followed by $b_1, \dots, b_k$, where every digit other than $1$ ends a run.

results.title: Binary run lengths
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the binary run lengths of $n$ form the list of the lengths of the maximal runs of $1$s in the binary expansion of $n$, in the order in which the runs occur when the digits are read from the least significant one. This is the paper's list $\mathcal{L}(n)$, whose order does not matter there; for $n = 0$ the list is empty.

results.title: Run length transform
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a sequence $S : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$, the run length transform of $S$ is the sequence $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ given by $T(n) = \prod_{\ell \in \mathcal{L}(n)} S(\ell)$, where $\mathcal{L}(n)$ is the list of the lengths of the maximal runs of $1$s in the binary expansion of $n$, so that each run contributes one factor.

results.title: Run length transform at zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every sequence $S : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$, the run length transform of $S$ takes the value $1$ at $0$, since $0$ has no runs of $1$s in binary.

results.title: Run length transform at eleven
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every sequence $S : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$, the run length transform $T$ of $S$ satisfies $T(11) = S(1) S(2)$: in binary $11$ is $1011$, whose maximal runs of $1$s have lengths $2$ and $1$.

results.title: Nonnegative discrete spectrum
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A nonnegative discrete spectrum is a sequence of real numbers $E_0, E_1, E_2, \ldots$, the eigenvalues listed with multiplicity, such that $E_j \ge 0$ for every $j$, $E_i \le E_j$ whenever $i \le j$, and $E_j \to +\infty$ as $j \to \infty$.

results.title: A nonnegative discrete spectrum is determined by its eigenvalues
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If two nonnegative discrete spectra $S$ and $T$ have the same $j$-th eigenvalue for every index $j \in \mathbb{N}$, then $S = T$.

results.title: Strict sublevel set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a nonnegative discrete spectrum with eigenvalues $E_0 \le E_1 \le \cdots$ and a real number $\Lambda$, the strict sublevel set at $\Lambda$ is the set of indices $\{j \in \mathbb{N} : E_j < \Lambda\}$.

results.title: Strict sublevel sets are finite
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a nonnegative discrete spectrum with eigenvalues $E_0 \le E_1 \le \cdots$ and every real number $\Lambda$, the strict sublevel set $\{j \in \mathbb{N} : E_j < \Lambda\}$ is finite.

results.title: Finite strict sublevel set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a nonnegative discrete spectrum with eigenvalues $E_0 \le E_1 \le \cdots$ and a real number $\Lambda$, the finite strict sublevel set at $\Lambda$ is the strict sublevel set $\{j \in \mathbb{N} : E_j < \Lambda\}$, regarded as a finite set of indices; it is finite because $E_j \to +\infty$.

results.title: Membership in the finite strict sublevel set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a nonnegative discrete spectrum with eigenvalues $E_0 \le E_1 \le \cdots$, a real number $\Lambda$ and an index $j \in \mathbb{N}$, the index $j$ lies in the finite strict sublevel set at $\Lambda$ if and only if $E_j < \Lambda$.

results.title: Eigenvalue counting function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a nonnegative discrete spectrum with eigenvalues $E_0 \le E_1 \le \cdots$ and a real number $\Lambda$, the counting function $N(\Lambda)$ is the number of indices $j \in \mathbb{N}$ with $E_j < \Lambda$, so eigenvalues are counted with multiplicity.

results.title: Riesz mean
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a nonnegative discrete spectrum with eigenvalues $E_0 \le E_1 \le \cdots$ and real numbers $\sigma$ and $\Lambda$, the Riesz mean of order $\sigma$ at $\Lambda$ is the finite sum $R_\sigma(\Lambda) = \sum_{j \in \mathbb{N},\, E_j < \Lambda} (\Lambda - E_j)^\sigma$ over indices, where $x^\sigma$ is the real power.

results.title: The Riesz mean of order zero is the counting function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a nonnegative discrete spectrum with eigenvalues $E_0 \le E_1 \le \cdots$ and every real number $\Lambda$, the Riesz mean of order $0$ at $\Lambda$ equals the counting function at $\Lambda$, viewed as a real number: $R_0(\Lambda) = N(\Lambda)$.

results.title: Fenchel conjugate
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real vector space with a topology and let $f : E \to [-\infty, \infty]$. The Fenchel conjugate of $f$ at a continuous linear functional $L : E \to \mathbb{R}$ is the extended real number $f^*(L) = \sup_{y \in E} \big(L(y) - f(y)\big)$.

results.title: Fenchel biconjugate
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real vector space with a topology and let $f : E \to [-\infty, \infty]$. results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Student's `t` law (Casella–Berger, Definition 5.3.4): for independent `Z ~ N(0, 1)` and `V ~ χ²_k` with `k ≥ 1`, `Z / √(V / k)` has density `Γ((k + 1)/2) / (√(k π) Γ(k/2)) · (1 + t²/k)^{-(k+1)/2}`.

results.summary: Snedecor's `F` law (Casella–Berger, Definition 5.3.6): for independent `V₁ ~ χ²_{d₁}` and `V₂ ~ χ²_{d₂}` with `d₁, d₂ ≥ 1`, `(V₁ / d₁) / (V₂ / d₂)` has density `Γ((d₁ + d₂)/2) / (Γ(d₁/2) Γ(d₂/2)) · (d₁/d₂)^{d₁/2} x^{d₁/2 - 1} (1 + d₁ x / d₂)^{-(d₁+d₂)/2}` on `x > 0`.

results.title: Hoeffding's central limit theorem

results.title: Graham's zero-sum statement (Erdős Problem 541)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: This is the statement that for every prime $p$ and every sequence $a_0, \dots, a_{p-1}$ of residues modulo $p$, not necessarily distinct, if there is a natural number $r$ such that every nonempty set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, p-1\}$ with $\sum_{i \in S} a_i = 0$ in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ has exactly $r$ elements, then at most two distinct residues occur among $a_0, \dots, a_{p-1}$.

results.title: Zero sums of a single length use at most two residues (Erdős Problem 541)

results.title: The ternary alphabet of Labbé's counterexample
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The alphabet is the three-letter set $\{0, 1, 2\}$.

results.title: Morphisms of the ternary alphabet
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A morphism of the ternary alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ is given by its letter map: a function $\varphi$ that sends each letter $a$ to a finite word $\varphi(a)$ over $\{0, 1, 2\}$, possibly the empty word.

results.title: Image of a word under a morphism
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A morphism $\varphi$ acts on a word $w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_k$ by $\varphi(w) = \varphi(w_1) \varphi(w_2) \cdots \varphi(w_k)$, the concatenation of the images of its letters; the empty word is sent to the empty word.

results.title: Iterated images of words under a morphism
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a morphism of the ternary alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$, acting on finite words letter by letter. Its iterates $\varphi^n$ on finite words are defined by $\varphi^0(w) = w$ and $\varphi^{n+1}(w) = \varphi(\varphi^n(w))$ for every natural number $n$ and every finite word $w$ over $\{0, 1, 2\}$.

results.title: Primitive morphisms
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a morphism of the ternary alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$, sending each letter to a finite word, and let $\varphi^n$ be the $n$-th iterate of its letter by letter extension to finite words, with $\varphi^0$ the identity. Then $\varphi$ is primitive when there is a natural number $n$ such that for all letters $a$ and $b$, the letter $b$ occurs in the word $\varphi^n(a)$.

results.title: Palindromes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite word $w$ over the alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ is a palindrome when it equals its reversal, that is, reads the same backwards; in particular the empty word is a palindrome.

results.title: Class P
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A morphism $\varphi$ is in class P (Hof–Knill–Simon) when there is a palindrome $p$ such that for every letter $a$, $\varphi(a) = p q_a$ for some palindrome $q_a$. The palindromes $p$ and $q_a$ may be empty.

results.title: Infinite words
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An infinite word over the alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ is a sequence $u = u_0 u_1 u_2 \cdots$ of letters indexed by the natural numbers, that is, a map $\mathbb{N} \to \{0, 1, 2\}$.

results.title: Occurrence of a word at a position
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite word $w = w_0 w_1 \cdots w_{n-1}$ over the ternary alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ occurs in an infinite word $u = u_0 u_1 u_2 \cdots$ over the same alphabet at position $k$ when $w_i = u_{k+i}$ for every $i < n$.

results.title: Factors of an infinite word
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite word $w$ is a factor of an infinite word $u$ when it occurs in $u$ at some position: there is $k \in \mathbb{N}$ with $w_i = u_{k+i}$ for every $i < |w|$ (letters of $w$ indexed from $0$). In particular the empty word is a factor of every infinite word.

results.title: Fixed point of a morphism
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An infinite word $u$ is a fixed point of a morphism $\varphi$ when it is the limit of the iterates of a prolongable letter: there is a letter $a$ such that $\varphi(a)$ begins with $a$, the words $\varphi^m(a)$ ($m \ge 0$) are arbitrarily long, and every $\varphi^m(a)$ is a prefix of $u$.

results.title: Palindromic infinite words
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An infinite word $u = u_0 u_1 u_2 \cdots$ over the ternary alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ is palindromic when it has arbitrarily long palindromic factors: for every natural number $N$ there is a finite word $w = w_0 \cdots w_{n-1}$ with $n \ge N$ that reads the same backwards and occurs in $u$: for some position $k$, $w_i = u_{k+i}$ for all $i < n$.

results.title: Conjugate morphisms
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\psi$ and $\theta$ be morphisms of the ternary alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$, each sending every letter to a finite word, and write $xy$ for the concatenation of words $x$ and $y$. Then $\psi$ and $\theta$ are conjugate when there is a finite word $w$ such that $\psi(a) w = w \theta(a)$ for every letter $a$, or there is a finite word $w$ such that $\theta(a) w = w \psi(a)$ for every letter $a$.

results.title: Identity morphism
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A morphism $\psi$ is the identity morphism when $\psi(a)$ is the one-letter word $a$ for every letter $a$.

results.title: Linear partition of a graph
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a vertex type $V$ and let $k$ be a natural number. A $k$-linear partition of $G$ is a set of exactly $k$ blocks, each block a nonempty finite sequence of pairwise distinct vertices, such that every vertex of $G$ lies in exactly one block and any two consecutive vertices of a block are nonadjacent in $G$. The blocks themselves are unordered; only the vertices within a block are ordered.

results.title: Encoded gates (Succinct Circuit Value)
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An encoded gate is a pair $(k, r)$ of a natural number $k$, the kind of the gate, and a list $r$ of natural numbers, its references.

results.title: Gate values of an encoded circuit (Succinct Circuit Value)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $C$ be a list of encoded gates, $a$ a list of booleans and $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Decode each gate of $C$ into a gate of a flat Boolean circuit on $n$ inputs, and assign to input $j < n$ the entry $a_j$ of $a$, read as false when $j$ is at least the length of $a$. The result is the list of the values of all gates of the decoded circuit under this assignment, in order.

results.title: Outputs of an encoded circuit (Succinct Circuit Value)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $C$ be a list of encoded gates, $a$ a list of booleans and $k, n \in \mathbb{N}$. Decode each gate of $C$ into a gate of a flat Boolean circuit on $n$ inputs and evaluate the decoded circuit with input $j < n$ set to the entry $a_j$ of $a$, read as false when $j$ is at least the length of $a$. The outputs of $C$ on $a$ are the last $k$ of the resulting gate values, or all of them if $C$ has fewer than $k$ gates.

results.title: Fixed-length binary expansion (Succinct Circuit Value)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $i$ and $n$, this is the list of $n$ booleans $(b_0, \dots, b_{n-1})$, least significant bit first, where $b_k$ is true exactly when $\lfloor i / 2^k \rfloor$ is odd. For $i < 2^n$ it is the $n$-bit binary expansion of $i$; in general it is the $n$-bit expansion of $i \bmod 2^n$.

results.title: Number with a given binary expansion (Succinct Circuit Value)
